Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS INSPECTION OCCURRED AT 6232 N. NORTHWEST HWY. AT THE 1ST FLOOR COMMERCIAL STOREFRONT / MERCHANTILE SPACE. THE INTERIOR OF THIS SPACE HAS BEEN EXTENSIVELY REHABBED AND IS NOT BEING USED AS ITS' ORIGINAL ZONING CERTIFICATION (MERCHANTILE SPACE).THERE ARE NEW PARTION WALLS FORMING ROOMS THAT INCLUDE AN OFFICE, GAMBLING ROOM(S), A FULL BATHROOM AND A FULLY APPOINTED KITCHEN. THERE IS ALL NEW ELECTRICAL - WIRING / PIPING / FIXTURES. THERE IS ALL NEW PLUMBING -  PIPING / FIXTURES. IN ADDITION TO THE PHYSICAL REHAB THERE IS A USE CHANGE FROM A MECHANTILE SPACE TO WHAT THE PROPRIETOR CALLS "A SOCIAL CLUB". THIS IS NOT PERMITTED BY THE CURRENT ZONING CERTIFICATION. THIS "SOCIAL CLUB" IS ACTUALLY AN ACTIVE GAMBLING VENUE WITH POKER TABLES, CRAPS (DICE) TABLES AND A LARGE BLACKBOARD WITH NAMES / SPORTS TEAMS DISPLAYED TRACKING SPORTING EVENTS. FOOD AND ALCOHOL ARE SERVED. THERE IS A COMMERCIAL GRADE CASH COUNTING MACHINE THERE AS WELL. THERE ARE NO LICENSES TO OPERATE AS EVEN A MERCHANTILE SPACE; NOR ARE THERE LICENSES FOR A SOCIAL CLUB OR GAMBLING / BETTING VENUE.THERE ARE NO PERMITS ON FILE FOR THE INTERIOR REHAB. PLANS AND A FULL RENO PERMIT ARE REQUIRED FOR THE FIRST FLOOR (6232) REHAB. ALSO, IF A ZONING CHANGE IS AUTHORIZED TO ALLOW FOR A "SOCIAL CLUB", THE LICENSE APPLICATION INVOLVES, NOT ONLY BACP, BUT ALSO THE DEPARTMENT OF BUILDINGS.SECTION 14A-4-401.1.

In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install and maintain approved smoke detectors. (13-196-100 thru 13-196-160) Install a smoke detector in every dwelling unit. Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Failed to rebuild or replace dilapidated and dangerous porch.  (13-196-570, 13-196-641)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS IS A DOUBLE WIDE (50'), 3 STORY REAR, OPEN FRAME WOOD PORCH. ALL OF THE STRUCTURAL COLUMNS ARE SET ON FOOTINGS OF AN UNDETERMINED DEPTH. AN EXAMINATION OF THESE FOOTINGS WILL BE REQUIRED. THE MAIN CENTER STAIR SYSTEM HAS OVER NOTCH CUT, SINGLE BOARD STAIR STRINGERS. THESE STAIR STRINGERS ARE NAILED, NOT BOLTED TO THE PORCH STRUCTURE. ALSO, THIS OUTRIGGER TYPE MAIN STAIR SYSTEM HAS SUPPORT COLUMNS THAT ARE OVER NOTCH CUT ON 2 COLUMN FACES IN ORDER TO RECIEVE THE STAIR LANDING RIM JOISTS. THIS FASTENING SYSTEM GREATLY REDUCES THE STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY OF THE SUPPORT COLUMNS. THE ENTIRE STAIR SYSTEM SWAYS LATERALLY UNDER LOAD. ALSO, ALL OF THE OTHER MAIN STRUCTURAL COLUMNS SUPPORTING EACH OF THE 3 LEVELS OF LARGE PORCH DECKS ARE OVER NOTCH CUT TO RECIEVE THE SUPPORT BEAMS. THESE STRUCTURAL JOINTS HAVE NO HEAVY DUTY METAL BRACKETS AT ANY OF THESE CRITICAL JOINTS. ALL OF THE COLUMN SECTIONS ARE JOINED WITH SUBSTANDARD 2 BOLT, 12" LAP JPOINTS.THERE ARE MISSING BANISTER PICKETS AT THE 2CD FLOOR STAIR LANDING. ALL OF THE MAIN PORCH DECKS (6 IN TOTAL) HAVE BANISTER SYSTEMS WITH UN-FASTENED BOTTOM RAILS THAT DEFLECT SEVERELY UNDER LOAD.THIS PORCH IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS IF OVERLOADED. THE STUCTURAL JOINERY IS WOEFULLY SUBSTANDARD AND PRESENTS A REAL TIME HAZARDOUS IF OVERLOADED. THE ORIGINAL COMPLAINT (311) ALLEDGED LARGE PARTIES BEING HELD ON THIS PORCH ON A REGULAR BASIS. THIS PORCH HAS BEEN POSTED AS DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS.THIS PORCH DOES NOT MEET MINIMUM CODE REQUIREMENTS IN SEVERAL AREAS. TO REPAIR THIS PORCH IN PLACE IS NOT A VIABLE OPTION. TEAR DOWN THIS PORCH  AND REPLACE WITH A NEW, STRUCTURALLY CODE COMPLIANT PORCH. ARCHITECTURAL PLANS AND A PERMIT ARE REQUIRED. SECTION 14X-5-505, 14X-3-303, 14X-12-1202, 14R-1-101, 14B-7-705, 14B-16-1604, 14X-3-305.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
